description: Leads interdisciplinary NEPA/permit teams where AI drafts, searches and sorts comments; owns scoping judgment, prompt/specification, validation and accountable sign-off; defends the record under shorter deadlines and a 150-day limitations period if SPEED Act passes. Needs FS-C01, FS-C03, FS-C09 plus core 6.1.4. Entry paths: NEPA specialists (0028/0401), consulting PMs, CAREP-type credential holders.

role_title: Environmental model risk and AI assurance officer
description: Inventories AI uses, classifies high-impact uses (OMB M-25-21), sets test and monitoring requirements, audits vendor models used in permitting, enforcement targeting and monitoring. Needs FS-C02, FS-C10, 7.1.4. Entry paths: data scientists (1560) with regulatory exposure, QA/QC leads, auditors; career move for senior analysts displaced by drafting automation.

Verification shifts from document audit to auditing remote-sensing models, sensor data and dynamic baselines, plus targeted field calibration; must quantify assessor variability. Needs FS-C07, FS-C08, 6.6.1. Entry paths: foresters, field ecologists and GHG accountants adding model-audit skills.

Designs and maintains field plots, labelled reference sets and regional validation for EO foundation models, dMRV and AI classifiers; decides where models are fit for use. Needs FS-C04, 2.2.3, 2.2.5, 4.1.1. Entry paths: field technicians and inventory crews (0404/0462), FIA-type programs; protects a field-craft ladder by giving it a data-craft destination.

24/7 fusion of satellite detection (FireSat-class), cameras, weather and fuels into decision support for initial attack, resource ordering and public warning; outside NWCG incident-only intelligence. Needs FS-C05, 4.3.4, 2.1.2. Entry paths: fire crews with GIS skills, IMETs, geospatial analysts, utility situational-awareness staff.

Evaluates, pilots, procures and scales detection, AI and aviation technologies; manages vendor data rights and training. Precedent: CAL FIRE Office of Wildfire Technology R&D. Needs FS-C10, FS-C09. Entry paths: fire management officers, aviation and IT program managers.

Owns a case-management or AI review product inside an agency: user research with reviewers, backlog, data-standard compliance, change management. Driven by CEQ data standard and Permitting Innovation Center; FAS/EPIC called for product managers. Needs FS-C09. Entry paths: experienced reviewers moving into product roles; digital-service staff gaining domain depth.

role_title: Drone and robotic operations program lead
description: Runs BVLOS fleets, airspace compliance, data pipelines and safety management once Part 108 lands; precursor is local drone-as-first-responder programs (>1,000 agencies on waivers). Needs FS-C06, 4.5.4, 4.4.1. Entry paths: UAS pilots, aviation managers, survey crews.

Maintains data assimilation, validation under nonstationarity, uncertainty communication and governance (incl. data sovereignty) for operational twins of watersheds, forests or fire. Currently research-stage. Needs FS-C11, 2.7.3. Entry paths: modelers, hydrologists, research-to-operations scientists.

role_title: Environmental AI evaluation and training expert
description: Domain experts design realistic multi-step environmental tasks and grading rubrics used to train and evaluate AI agents (posting requires 3+ years at agency/consultancy; ~USD 1,150-1,450 per task). Needs FS-C17. Entry paths: experienced and recently displaced agency and consulting staff. Ambivalent: builds the systems that may substitute for entry work.

Negotiates and administers co-stewardship, Good Neighbor, 638 and state-based leadership agreements as management devolves; tracks obligations, funding and performance. Needs FS-C14, 6.5.1, 6.5.3. Entry paths: Tribal liaisons, grants and agreements specialists (1109), state forestry staff.

Runs structured tacit-knowledge elicitation, paired work and field-walk capture with departing experts; maintains communities of practice and re-employed annuitant programs. Needs FS-C12, 7.2.2. Entry paths: senior practitioners, training officers, knowledge managers.

role_title: Corporate GHG and nature data controller
description: Owns auditable Scope 1-3 and nature-related data for SB 253 (first reports 10 Nov 2026), ESRS and ISSB-aligned regimes; narrative reporting roles shrink as standards simplify and templatize. Needs FS-C18, 6.6.1. Entry paths: accountants, environmental compliance staff, EHS managers.

Assesses business dependencies and impacts on biodiversity, structures nature-credit and blended-finance deals; legitimized by IPBES Business and Biodiversity Assessment. Needs 6.6.2, 6.6.4, FS-C07. Entry paths: ecologists with finance training, ESG analysts.

Helps communities and small jurisdictions translate hazard data into funded adaptation options as federal technical assistance thins and data moves to NGOs. Needs FS-C16, 1.5.3. Entry paths: planners, extension agents, floodplain managers, AmeriCorps alumni.

Coordinates volunteer data with AI-assisted identification and automated QA; becomes a capacity substitute where paid monitoring is cut. Needs 5.4.4, FS-C08. Entry paths: educators, volunteer managers, field technicians. Confirm with posting data.

role_title: Administrative record and AI provenance specialist
description: Assembles litigation-ready records documenting which analyses were AI-assisted, data lineage and human review, under shorter limitations periods and 'substantive comment' rules. Needs FS-C03. Entry paths: paralegals, records managers, NEPA coordinators. Speculative until courts rule on AI-assisted records.

The P-position learning substrate (drafting, literature and document review, comment coding) is being automated first in consulting and agencies; v1 rates CLD 'Highest' on 6.1.1, 6.1.2, 6.4.1, 6.4.4. Without redesign, few will reach review-and-certify competence.

role_title: Conservation corps, internship and seasonal crew member
description: Paid internships -43.8% and AmeriCorps -42% in 2025 postings; USD 400m AmeriCorps cuts; this is the main entry ladder for field craft and a diversity pipeline.

BLM, NPS, BIA, FWS fire programs consolidating into the U.S. Wildland Fire Service (~4,000 permanent staff); USFS merger blocked pending feasibility study. Qualification and classification will be redesigned.

role_title: Utility fire-weather and wildfire risk specialist
description: Utility situational-awareness centers hire meteorologists for fire-weather forecasting, PSPS and model development (WRF, Python); competes with NWS/IMET and agency talent.

As USFS moves to state-based leadership models and partners take on management, state staff need federal-equivalent NEPA, sale-prep, consultation and agreement competencies without federal training pipelines.
EO embeddings and AI classification compress routine mapping and change detection; work shifts to validation, labels and interpretation (v1 2.1.1 and 2.1.2 modal Ac; 2.1.2 S-trajectory).
AI theme and sentiment sorting of comments already in consulting use; remaining human work is judging substantive comments and responding.
Species ID moves to automated classifiers and molecular assays; analyst role becomes sample design, chain of custody and classifier QA (v1 2.6.2 modal V; 1.6.2 S-trajectory).
Data-centre and generation siting adds water-rights, transmission and community-consent review load to environmental and Tribal staff.
Federal EJ positions selectively left on leave or eliminated; capacity migrating to state programs and community organizations (refugia).
